usual_baseline: Handwritten notes are complete for basics such as date, surgeon and procedure, usually 95–100%. They are weak on tourniquet time (20% [1136], 32% [1285]), closure (16% [1285], 16.99% [1423]), blood loss (7% [1136]) and post-op instructions (24% [1285], 40% [1136]). Overall scores ran from 50% [1382] to 58.7% [1235].
fix_that_works: Typed or electronic templates give the biggest gains. GIRFT hip proforma: 50% to 92% [1382]. Smart e-note: closure 60% to 100% and antibiotics 69% to 100% [1272]. Typed template: post-op instructions 40% to 92% [1136]. Digital template: missing parameters fell from 10 to 3 [533]. Presenting results and giving senior feedback: blood loss 0% to 28.6% and findings 34% to 74.3% [1538].
fix_that_fails: Blood loss stayed at 8% despite a typed template [1136]. A mixed bundle left mean compliance at 82.0% to 83.4%, and prosthesis documentation fell from 87% to 26.1% [1504]. Annual teaching gave small gains that plateaued, with suture details at 41.5% [1398]. Closure was 16.99% even on a typed EMR form [1423]. Elective/emergency status stayed at 31.4% [1538].
consultant_advice: This audit is heavily overdone, and the result is predictable: templates work and teaching gives small gains. Only choose it if you can change the electronic template itself. Measure the fields that are not mandated, such as closure, blood loss and VTE plan, and check that the template has not made other fields worse [1504].
